_readme: Copy this file to app/data/alerts.json to turn on phone alerts. It lives
here rather than beside the app because app/data/ is gitignored, and a
template nobody can find is a feature nobody switches on. Until you copy
it, the
only destination is the Windows toast on this machine, and everything else
is recorded and waits. That default is deliberate: an alert names your
symbol, your direction and your P&L, so sending it anywhere off this PC
hands that to somebody else's server. That is your call to make.
ntfy.sh needs no account. Pick a LONG random topic and treat it as a
password — anyone who knows the topic can read every alert you send to it.
Install the ntfy app on the phone and subscribe to the same topic.
loud_only:true withholds the quiet channel from that sink. Worth using:
drift alerts run 13-44 a day against 2-8 setup announcements and land in
every hour including overnight, and the code that raises them calls them
awareness rather than something to act on. Three alerts you can act on,
buried under thirty you cannot, is the failure this avoids.
heartbeat_url is checked every 5 minutes and is the only alert that can
survive this machine dying. Nothing running here can report its own death
— point it at a service that alarms when the pings STOP (healthchecks.io
and cronitor both have free tiers) and that is the one that reaches you
when the PC is the thing that failed.
